note: Thirty-nine measured regions resolve to sixteen figure items, twelve table blocks and eleven exclusions. The exclusions are all photographs set inside a table: three in Table 1 on p7, four in its p8 half, two in Table 2 and two in Table 3. Twelve table blocks carry only nine printed labels because Tables 1, 7 and 11 each break over a page turn and the second half prints without a caption. The paper prints no Table 4 and no Table 10. p35 measures as one block but prints two figures, recorded as one item with the second plot named in the note; the in-text reference to '(Figure 1)' on p31 is a misnumber for Fig. 14 and is left as printed.
rules: Leaf-shape plots are recorded as line only where the crop shows a coordinate frame; the silhouette and phyllotaxy figures carry no axes [geometry.printed_numbers].
Multi-panel figures of one family keep that family and carry the panel count instead of being recorded as composite-panel [geometry.panel_count].

Illustrations embedded inside a table are measured as their own raster blocks but are part of the table above them, so they are excluded rather than counted as photo-or-raster-image exhibits [geometry.family].
All twelve table blocks are fully gridded, so rule_style is boxed [table.rule_style].
Three tables print in two halves across a page break; the second half is recorded with continued true and the label of the half it belongs to [table.continued].
The paper prints labels 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9 and 11 only; there is no Table 4 or Table 10 anywhere, and the numbering is not a census artefact [caption.numbering].
Captions sit above the table and below the figure throughout, so caption.position follows the printed side rather than the lane default [caption.position].
The p35 block is a single drawing cluster holding both Figure 15 and Figure 16, so it is recorded once, with the second plot named in the note [caption.verbatim].
The three continuation halves repeat no header row on the page, but header_rows cannot fall below one, so each keeps 1 and its note says the header sits on the previous page [table.header_rows].
